text:
+János Reviewers need to use as good a stable build for the rest of the parts as they can. While it could skew results away from what a consumer will get, which is a valid criticism of such a setup, you get a really good view of the quality of the card itself, which is the point of a benchmark. The performance hits you'll see on lower end CPUs won't be consistent across different CPU/GPU setups, so it wouldn't be an accurate representation of how the GPUs stack up against each other.

What I mean by this is, let's say the 480 loses 20% of its FPS on a 3rd gen i5, while a 1070 loses 10%. On a 4th gen i5 the 480 might lose 5% of its FPS while the Nvidia card might lose 10% anyway. This will heavily skew results in an industry where they're already so finnicky due to marketing ploys.

When you're dealing with reviewing it's best to ensure the bottleneck is with the part you're reviewing, that way you get a good gauge of the upper limit of that part. Can it, in some cases, be a let down to somebody buying a card like this? Sure. But it's entirely the purchaser's fault if they're shoving a 480 into a machine with a Core 2 duo processor. If you don't know where your bottleneck is and you buy a graphics card expecting to get the full performance out of your card that's not the reviewer's fault.

Though for a middleground I would have liked to see the reviews on a 6600k as the i7 is very unlikely to be as widespread as the i5 6600k, and the 6600k is definitely going to be the processor of choice for most 480, 1070 and 1060 builds going forward.

All NVIDIA fanboys, please read-
1. The rx 480 came out just a few days ago. The Gtx 970 had so much more time to mature with drivers. 
2. This is a reference rx 480 with limited stock cooling. Overclocking is therefore limited. The Gtx 970 in this video is factory overclocked with a lot more efficient cooling. Hence the overclock. headroom. 
3. The 200$ rx480 has a full 4Gb vram buffer whereas the more expensive gtx970 has 3.5 gigs +0.5 slower vram. 
4. The Gtx 970 lacks the asynchronous compute technology that hinders its directX 12 performance. The rx480 is much more future proof than the gtx 970. 
5. As more dx12 games roll out to the shelves, the gtx 970 will become increasingly inefficient in playing them. On the other hand, the rx480 performance will see increase in performance for quite some time. 
6. Console ports to the PC will see better ports to the rx480 as the mid gen consoled(aka neo and scorpio) will use gpus similar to the rx480 (ie polaris).

1. Add a smaller SSD (If not now, then later)
for Windows. Your PC will start up in seconds.
